# Auth epic — feature contract (frozen for execution run 1)

**Status:** frozen. Implementers do not edit this file; see [`docs/shared-contract.md`](../../shared-contract.md)
§4 for the amendment protocol.
**Covers:** [AUTH-001](../AUTH-001-auth-registration/story.md) ·
[AUTH-002](../AUTH-002-auth-login/story.md) ·
[AUTH-003](../AUTH-003-auth-session-refresh-logout/story.md), plus the FR-20..24 gateway
chain and the `GET /users/me` session probe LAND-001 depends on.
**Not covered by run 1:** AUTH-004 (session list/revoke) and AUTH-005 (admin) — run 2.
Their storage columns exist from run 1 so run 2 adds no breaking migration.
**Source spec:** [`docs/srs-authentication.md`](../../srs-authentication.md) (SRS-AUTH-001).
Where this contract and the SRS disagree on a *detail*, this contract wins for run 1 and the
divergence is recorded in §0. Where they disagree on a *requirement*, the SRS wins and this
contract is wrong — escalate.

---

## 0. Decisions taken before the freeze

Four questions the repo's own documents flagged as "decide before implementing Phase 2".
Decided by the instructor with the repo owner, 2026-09-07.

### D1 — Run 1 is the spine: AUTH-001, AUTH-002, AUTH-003

Registration (local + Google), login, refresh/rotation/logout, the gateway check chain, and
the SPA's real HTTP client. Session listing (AUTH-004) and admin (AUTH-005) are run 2. The
`auth.users.status` column and the `AccountStatus` enum ship in run 1 so that login can honour
suspension (D2) before anything can set it.

### D2 — A suspended account is told so, but only after its password verifies

Resolves the open tension in [`audit-and-errors.md`](../../audit-and-errors.md) §7
(option 3 of the three listed there).

`POST /auth/login` verifies the password **first**. Only when the credentials are correct and
the account is suspended does it return `403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`. A wrong password on a
suspended account is indistinguishable from a wrong password on an active one, and from an
unknown address: `401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

Why: FR-42 wants a suspended user to learn why they cannot get in; FR-08/FR-14 want no
enumeration oracle. Gating the distinct code behind a correct password gives the real owner
the explanation and gives a prober nothing they did not already have — they must already hold
the password. It still leaks to a credential-stuffer holding a valid pair; that is accepted,
recorded here, and is the residual risk of this option.

Consequence for the model: `LoginFailureReason.account_suspended` is **retained but no longer
emitted** (its compact DB code is permanent and must not be retired for a live value — see
`audit-and-errors.md` §6). The suspended outcome gets its own event, `auth.login.suspended`,
because an event carries exactly one `error_code` and this outcome's code differs from
`auth.login.failed`'s.

### D3 — A breached password is rejected; an unreachable HIBP fails open

FR-02 (Priority S) left "warn or reject" open. Registration and password-reset-confirm reject
a password found in the HIBP k-anonymity corpus with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` and
`field: "password"`, `rule: "breached"`.

If the HIBP endpoint errors or exceeds its timeout (default 2s), the check is **skipped** and
the request proceeds, with a `warn` line in the operational log. Local development and an HIBP
outage must never block signup (AUTH-001 story, dependencies). `AUTH_HIBP_ENABLED=false`
disables the check outright; the compose file sets it false.

### D4 — "Unverified is read-only" is enforced once, in the gateway

FR-03 never said where. It is one middleware stage (§6), driven by an `email_verified` claim
in the access token, rejecting unsafe methods with `403 AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED`. Per-service
checks were rejected: the rule would be re-decided by every future domain, and one that forgets
it fails open silently.

### D5 — Every response is enveloped, including the ones LAND-001 froze unenveloped

This is a **contract amendment to [LAND-001](../LAND-001-public-landing-page/contract.md) §1**,
raised by the instructor, not by an executor.

LAND-001 was written before `libs/httpkit/envelope.go` existed and specified bare bodies
(`202 {"status":"pending_verification"}`, `200 {"csrf_token": "..."}`). The standing policy in
`shared-contract.md` §3 — every body enveloped, no exceptions — post-dates it and wins. All
run-1 success bodies are `{"data": ...}`. `204 No Content` responses carry no body at all,
which is not an exception to the envelope so much as an absence of one.

**Affected finished work:** `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts` (the mock) and `auth.types.ts`. Slice
`fe-auth-client` re-verifies both against this shape; the mock is updated to envelope its
responses so mock and real clients stay swap-compatible. No component changes — components
never see the envelope.

### D6 — `GET /users/me` is served by the auth package

LAND-001 §0.2 added this endpoint and assigned it to "user-service". Every field it returns is
auth-owned (`id`, `email`, `role`) except `tier`, which belongs to the subscription domain and
does not exist yet — it is a hardcoded `"free"` with a `TODO` naming the domain that will own
it. The response also re-issues the session-bound CSRF token, which is session state.

So the handler lives in `internal/auth/session/` and is registered at the frozen public path
`/api/v1/users/me`. Path and owner deliberately differ; both are recorded here and flagged for
`docs/backend.md` §2 and the SRS at integration. Creating a `user` package that reads
`auth.users` to serve one stubbed field would be the actual ownership violation.

### D7 — `/auth/refresh` is exempt from CSRF; every other state-changing auth call is not

The SPA holds the CSRF token in memory only. After a reload with an expired access token, the
boot sequence is refresh → `/users/me`, and the token needed to satisfy CSRF is only available
*after* that. Requiring CSRF on refresh deadlocks the boot path.

Refresh is protected instead by the refresh cookie's own properties: `SameSite=Lax` means a
browser does not attach it to a cross-site `POST` at all, and `Path=/api/v1/auth` keeps it off
every other endpoint. Rotation plus replay detection (FR-31) means a forged refresh that did
somehow land is a one-shot that kills the session it stole. `/auth/logout`, `/auth/logout-all`
and every non-auth unsafe request still require `X-CSRF-Token`.

## 1. HTTP surface

Base path `/api/v1`. Every request carries `Accept-Language`; the server renders `message` from
`libs/i18n/locales/` (`audit-and-errors.md` §1a). Error envelope
`{"error": {"code", "message"}}`, success envelope `{"data": ...}`, both written only through
`libs/httpkit`. Codes are the generated `ErrorCode` union — no others exist.

| # | Endpoint | Method | Auth | Request | Success | Errors (status → code) | FR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/auth/register` | POST | none | `{email, password}` | **202** `{"data":{"status":"pending_verification"}}` — byte-identical whether or not the email exists; **no cookies** | 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`; 429 `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | 01,02,04,08 |
| 2 | `/auth/verify-email` | POST | none | `{token}` | **200** `{"data":{"status":"verified"}}` | 400 `AUTH_LINK_INVALID`; 429 `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | 03 |
| 3 | `/auth/password-reset/request` | POST | none | `{email}` | **202** `{"data":{"status":"sent"}}` — byte-identical for an unknown address; no mail sent | 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`; 429 `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | 07,08 |
| 4 | `/auth/password-reset/confirm` | POST | none | `{token, password}` | **200** `{"data":{"status":"reset"}}` + epoch advanced | 400 `AUTH_LINK_INVALID`; 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`; 429 `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` | 07 |
| 5 | `/auth/oauth/google` | GET (navigation) | none | — | **302** to Google consent; sets `gs_oauth_state` cookie | — | 05 |
| 6 | `/auth/oauth/google/callback` | GET (navigation) | none | `?code&state` | **302 → `/dashboard`** + session cookies | **302 → `/?auth_error=oauth_cancelled`** on denial; **302 → `/?auth_error=oauth_link_required`** when the email matches a local account (§4.3); **302 → `/?auth_error=oauth_failed`** on a bad `state`/PKCE. Never a JSON body — this is a browser navigation | 05,06 |
| 7 | `/auth/oauth/link/confirm` | POST | none | `{token}` | **200** `{"data":{"status":"linked"}}` | 400 `AUTH_LINK_INVALID` | 06 |
| 8 | `/auth/login` | POST | none | `{email, password}` | **200** `{"data":{"csrf_token": string}}` + both cookies | 401 `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`; 403 `AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` (**only after the password verifies**, D2); 429 `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` + `Retry-After: <seconds>`; 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 10..14 |
| 9 | `/auth/refresh` | POST | refresh cookie | — | **200** `{"data":{"csrf_token": string}}` + rotated cookies | 401 `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`; 401 `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED`; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (Redis down — fail closed) | 30,31,34 |
| 10 | `/auth/logout` | POST | access + CSRF | — | **204**, both cookies cleared | 401 `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`; 403 `AUTH_CSRF_FAILED`; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | 32 |
| 11 | `/auth/logout-all` | POST | access + CSRF | — | **204**, both cookies cleared | as above | 33 |
| 12 | `/users/me` | GET | access | — | **200** `{"data":{"user":{id,email,role,tier}, "csrf_token": string}}` | 401 `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`; 401 `AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED` | LAND-001 §0.2/§0.4, D6 |

### 1.1 Rules that bind both sides

- **Enumeration-neutral pairs must be byte-identical**, not merely similar: same status, same
  body bytes, same headers modulo `Date`. #1 for a new vs. taken address; #3 for a real vs.
  unknown address; #8's `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for unknown-email vs. bad-password. Timing
  is equalised by always performing an argon2id verification — against a fixed dummy hash when
  the account does not exist — so an unknown address costs the same as a wrong password.
- **`VALIDATION_FAILED` payload:** `{"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_FAILED","message":"...",
  "details":[{"field":"password","rule":"min_length"}]}}`. `details` is additive to the
  envelope and optional; clients must tolerate its absence. Rules used in run 1: `min_length`,
  `format`, `breached`.
- **Never a token string in a body, URL, log or non-httpOnly store.** The CSRF token is not a
  token in this sense — it is bound to the session and useless without the cookies.
- The effective user ID always comes from the token, never from the request.

## 2. Tokens, cookies, CSRF

### 2.1 Claims

```
access  { sub, sid, role, tier, email_verified, jti, iat, exp, typ:"access" }   TTL 15m
refresh { sub, sid,                             jti, iat, exp, typ:"refresh" }  TTL 30d absolute
```

RS256, `kid` in the header, two-key verification window for rotation (SEC-02). `sid` is the
**session** id — stable across every rotation within one login, and the key the session record,
the CSRF token and (in run 2) session revocation are all addressed by. `jti` is the token id —
new on every mint, and the unit of blacklisting.

`typ` is checked: an access token presented to `/auth/refresh` is rejected, and a refresh token
presented as an access token is rejected, before any other check.

### 2.2 Cookies

| Cookie | Value | Path | Attributes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gs_access` | access JWT | `/` | `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=900` |
| `gs_refresh` | refresh JWT | `/api/v1/auth` | `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=2592000` |
| `gs_oauth_state` | state+PKCE verifier, signed | `/api/v1/auth/oauth` | `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=600` |

`Secure` is emitted unless `AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=false`, which exists **only** so local compose
over plain http works. It is true by default and in every deployed environment; a test asserting
cookie attributes asserts the default.

### 2.3 CSRF (FR-24)

Issued at login and re-issued by `/users/me` and `/auth/refresh`: 32 random bytes,
base64url, stored in the session record, returned in the body, held by the SPA in memory only.

Required on every `POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` **except** the unauthenticated auth endpoints
(#1–#7, which have no session to bind to) and `/auth/refresh` (D7). Mismatch or absence →
`403 AUTH_CSRF_FAILED`. Comparison is constant-time.

---

## 3. Redis keys

The gateway and the auth package are the only readers/writers. Every key is namespaced and
every key carries a TTL — nothing here requires a cleanup job (NFR-03).

| Key | Type | Value | TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blacklist:{jti}` | string | `"1"` | the token's **remaining** life, computed from `exp` — never a constant |
| `user_blacklist_epoch:{user_id}` | string | unix seconds | 30d, refreshed on write |
| `user_sessions:{user_id}` | hash | field `sid` → JSON `{sid, refresh_jti, device_label, created_at, last_seen_at, csrf_token}` | 30d, refreshed on write |
| `login_fail:{user_id}` | string | consecutive failure count | 15m sliding |
| `login_fail_ip:{ip}` | string | consecutive failure count | 15m sliding |
| `login_backoff:{user_id}` | string | backoff step `n` | the current delay, `30 * 2^(n-1)` seconds, capped at 3600 |
| `ratelimit:{scope}:{key}` | string | token-bucket counter | window length |

**Epoch check:** a token is stale when `iat < epoch`. Because `iat` has second resolution, a
token minted in the same second as an epoch write would survive; `logout-all` therefore writes
`epoch = now + 1`, which is why AUTH-003's scenario "including the legitimately-rotated one just
issued" holds.

**Backoff (FR-13):** the counter is per *account*, which is what makes AUTH-002's "backoff
blocks the account even from a new source IP" true; `login_fail_ip` is a second, independent
control and neither substitutes for the other. The 5th consecutive failure sets
`login_backoff` to step 1 (30s); each further failure after a served window increments the step,
so delays go 30, 60, 120… A successful login deletes all three keys.

**Idle expiry (FR-34):** `now - last_seen_at > 14d` → `401 AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRED`. `last_seen_at`
is written on every successful refresh, not on every request — a per-request Redis write on the
hot path is exactly what NFR-01 budgets against.

## 4. Postgres

One migration series, `infra/db/migrations/NNNN_*.up.sql` / `.down.sql`, single-writer
(`backend.md` §3). Schemas: `auth` (this epic) and `audit` (platform).

Every column storing an enum stores the **compact 8-char code**
(`audit-and-errors.md` §6), typed `char(8)`, never the readable string.

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA auth;
CREATE SCHEMA audit;

CREATE TABLE auth.users (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  email           text        NOT NULL,              -- as the user typed it
  email_lower     text        NOT NULL UNIQUE,       -- FR-01 case-insensitive uniqueness
  password_hash   text        NULL,                  -- NULL for OAuth-only accounts
  role            char(8)     NOT NULL,              -- Role, compact
  status          char(8)     NOT NULL,              -- AccountStatus, compact (run 2 writes it)
  email_verified_at timestamptz NULL,
  created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE auth.oauth_identities (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provider    char(8)     NOT NULL,                  -- LinkedProvider, compact
  subject     text        NOT NULL,                  -- provider's stable subject claim
  email       text        NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (provider, subject)
);

-- One table for all three single-use emailed links (SEC-04). Only the hash is stored.
CREATE TABLE auth.link_tokens (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind        char(8)     NOT NULL,                  -- LinkKind, compact
  token_hash  bytea       NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- sha256 of the emailed token
  expires_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
  consumed_at timestamptz NULL,
  payload     jsonb       NULL,                      -- oauth_link: {provider, subject, email}
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON auth.link_tokens (user_id, kind);

-- Append-only (FR-45, SEC-07). The application's DB role is granted INSERT and SELECT only;
-- no API path updates or deletes a row here.
CREATE TABLE audit.records (
  id             bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  occurred_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  event_code     char(8)     NOT NULL,               -- compact audit-event code
  actor_type     char(8)     NOT NULL,               -- ActorType, compact
  outcome        char(8)     NOT NULL,               -- Outcome, compact
  severity       char(8)     NOT NULL,               -- Severity, compact
  actor_user_id  uuid        NULL,
  target_user_id uuid        NULL,
  request_id     text        NULL,
  fields         jsonb       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  message        text        NOT NULL                -- rendered en-US, always
);
CREATE INDEX ON audit.records (occurred_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ON audit.records (target_user_id, occurred_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ON audit.records (event_code, occurred_at DESC);
```

Migrations are never applied by application startup (`backend.md` §3); `cmd/migrate` is a
separate binary with `up`, `down` and `status`.

### 4.3 OAuth linking (FR-06)

The callback finds a Google identity whose email matches an existing local account and no
`oauth_identities` row:

1. No session is issued and nothing is merged.
2. A `LinkKind.oauth_link` row is written to `auth.link_tokens` (1h expiry) with the provider,
   subject and email in `payload`, and the token is **emailed to the account's address** — the
   verified-email half of FR-06's "login or verified-email confirmation".
3. The browser is redirected to `/?auth_error=oauth_link_required`.
4. `POST /auth/oauth/link/confirm {token}` consumes it, writes the `oauth_identities` row, and
   returns 200. It issues no session — the user then logs in normally.

The token is emailed rather than put in the redirect URL on purpose: a single-use credential in
a query string lands in browser history, referrers and any proxy log in between.

## 5. Go seams

Cross-slice types and interfaces live in **`services/monolith/internal/auth/authdomain/`**,
written by the `be-auth-store` slice from this section and imported by every later backend
slice. No wave-3 slice imports another wave-3 slice's package; concrete types meet at the
composition root.

```go
package authdomain

type Account struct {
    ID              uuid.UUID
    Email           string
    EmailLower      string
    PasswordHash    string      // "" for OAuth-only accounts
    Role            auditmodel.Role
    Status          auditmodel.AccountStatus
    EmailVerifiedAt *time.Time
    CreatedAt       time.Time
}

func (a Account) IsVerified() bool  { return a.EmailVerifiedAt != nil }
func (a Account) IsSuspended() bool { return a.Status == auditmodel.AccountStatusSuspended }

type AccountRepo interface {
    ByEmail(ctx context.Context, emailLower string) (*Account, error) // (nil, nil) when absent
    ByID(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (*Account, error)
    Create(ctx context.Context, a Account) error                      // ErrEmailTaken on conflict
    SetPasswordHash(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID, hash string) error
    MarkEmailVerified(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID, at time.Time) error
}

type OAuthIdentityRepo interface {
    BySubject(ctx context.Context, provider auditmodel.LinkedProvider, subject string) (*Account, error)
    Link(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID, provider auditmodel.LinkedProvider, subject, email string) error
}

type LinkTokenRepo interface {
    // Issue returns the RAW token to email; only its hash is stored.
    Issue(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID, kind auditmodel.LinkKind, ttl time.Duration, payload any) (string, error)
    // Consume validates and marks used in one atomic step. Returns ErrLinkInvalid for
    // unknown, expired or already-consumed tokens — the caller must not distinguish them.
    Consume(ctx context.Context, kind auditmodel.LinkKind, raw string) (*LinkToken, error)
}

// Implemented by the session slice, consumed by credentials/oauth at the composition root.
type SessionIssuer interface {
    // Issue mints a pair, writes the session record and returns the CSRF token. It sets
    // cookies on w. It never decides whether the caller *may* log in.
    Issue(ctx context.Context, w http.ResponseWriter, a Account, userAgent, sourceIP string) (csrfToken string, err error)
    RevokeAll(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) error // epoch advance; FR-33
}

// Implemented by the credentials slice, consumed by oauth.
type AccountProvisioner interface {
    // ProvisionFromOAuth returns the existing account for this identity, or creates one with
    // role User and a verified email. Returns ErrLinkRequired when a local account owns the
    // address and no identity row exists (FR-06).
    ProvisionFromOAuth(ctx context.Context, provider auditmodel.LinkedProvider, subject, email string) (*Account, error)
}

var (
    ErrEmailTaken   = errors.New("authdomain: email taken")
    ErrLinkInvalid  = errors.New("authdomain: link token invalid")
    ErrLinkRequired = errors.New("authdomain: oauth link requires proof of control")
    ErrNotFound     = errors.New("authdomain: not found")
)
```

**Route registration.** Each backend slice exports exactly one registrar; the composition root
calls them and no slice touches another's routes.

```go
func (h *CredentialsHandler) Register(r gin.IRouter)  // #1,2,3,4,7
func (h *OAuthHandler) Register(r gin.IRouter)        // #5,6
func (h *SessionHandler) Register(r gin.IRouter)      // #8,9,10,11 and /users/me
```

**Signing keys.** `libs/authmw` loads an RS256 keypair: `AUTH_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`,
`AUTH_JWT_PUBLIC_KEYS_PATH` (a directory of `<kid>.pub`, so two keys can verify while one
signs). Local dev keys are generated by `infra/db/../scripts` — see the `be-wiring` brief — and
are git-ignored (SEC-06).

## 6. Gateway middleware chain

`gateway.New` already reserves the stage order (GATE-001). Run 1 fills it:

```
recovery → request ID → logging → CORS → locale →
rate limit → auth → CSRF → verified-write → role → handler
```

- **auth (FR-20)** — checks, in this exact order, and records the **first** failure as the
  `TokenRejectReason`: signature → expiry → `blacklist:{jti}` → `iat` vs epoch. Every failure
  returns `401 AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` regardless of which check failed. Public routes are opted out
  by route group, not by the middleware inspecting paths.
- **CSRF (FR-24)** — §2.3.
- **verified-write (FR-03, D4)** — unsafe method + `email_verified=false` → `403
  AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED`, except under `/api/v1/auth/`.
- **role (FR-22)** — `RequireRole(system_admin)` returns `403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN`, never 404. Run 1
  ships the middleware and its tests; run 2 is what mounts routes behind it.
- **degradation (NFR-02)** — when Redis is unreachable: safe methods (GET/HEAD) proceed on
  signature+expiry alone and log at `warn`; everything else, including `/auth/refresh` and
  `/auth/logout*`, returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and logs at `error`.
- **rate limit (NFR-04)** — `login` 10/min per IP and per account; `register` 5/min per IP;
  `password-reset/*` 5/min per IP and per account; `verify-email` and `oauth/link/confirm`
  10/min per IP; `refresh` 60/min per session. Exceeded → `429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` with
  `Retry-After`.

**Downstream packages verify signature and expiry only and never call Redis (FR-21).** In the
monolith this is a rule about which helper a handler calls: `authmw.ClaimsFromContext(c)` reads
what the gateway already validated. A domain package importing the Redis client for an auth
decision is the violation this contract exists to prevent.

---

## 7. Model additions (`libs/auditmodel/model.yaml`)

Owned exclusively by the `plat-audit-model` slice. Everything else consumes the generated
output. Additive only — no existing key is renamed and no compact code is retired.

**Enums**

```yaml
AccountStatus:      { active, suspended }
LinkKind:           { email_verification, password_reset, oauth_link }
LinkRejectReason:   { unknown, expired, already_consumed }
```

**Error codes**

| Code | Status | For |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED` | 403 | D4 — an unverified account attempted a write |
| `AUTH_LINK_INVALID` | 400 | A verification / reset / oauth-link token that is unknown, expired **or** already used — deliberately one code, for the same reason `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` is one code |

**Events**

| Event | Actor | Outcome | Severity | Fields | Error code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.login.suspended` | anonymous | denied | warn | `user_id`, `source_ip` | `AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` |
| `auth.email.verified` | user | success | info | `user_id` | — |
| `auth.link.rejected` | anonymous | failure | warn | `kind` (LinkKind), `reason` (LinkRejectReason), `user_id?`, `source_ip` | `AUTH_LINK_INVALID` |
| `auth.password_reset.requested` | anonymous | success | info | `user_id?` (absent for an unknown address), `source_ip` | — |
| `auth.oauth.link_required` | anonymous | denied | warn | `user_id`, `provider` (LinkedProvider), `source_ip` | — |
| `auth.write_blocked_unverified` | user | denied | info | `user_id`, `path`, `request_id` | `AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED` |

`LoginFailureReason.account_suspended` gains a `note:` recording that D2 retired its use; the
value itself stays (its compact code is permanent).

## 8. Frontend contract

### 8.1 `apps/web/src/api/auth.types.ts` — additive changes

```ts
export interface VerifyEmailRequest { token: string }
export interface PasswordResetRequestRequest { email: string }
export interface PasswordResetConfirmRequest { token: string; password: string }
export interface OAuthLinkConfirmRequest { token: string }
export interface StatusResponse { status: string }

export interface ValidationDetail { field: string; rule: string }
// ApiError gains: details?: ValidationDetail[]

export interface AuthApi {
  // ...existing five members, unchanged in signature...
  verifyEmail(req: VerifyEmailRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<StatusResponse>;
  requestPasswordReset(req: PasswordResetRequestRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<StatusResponse>;
  confirmPasswordReset(req: PasswordResetConfirmRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<StatusResponse>;
  confirmOAuthLink(req: OAuthLinkConfirmRequest, opts?: RequestOptions): Promise<StatusResponse>;
}
```

`register`, `login`, `logout`, `me`, `googleAuthorizeUrl` keep their signatures. Their
**transport** changes per D5 — every success body is unwrapped from `{data: ...}` inside
`auth.ts` — so no component changes.

### 8.2 Client obligations

- `Accept-Language: <i18n.resolvedLanguage>` and `credentials: "include"` on every request.
- `X-CSRF-Token` on every unsafe request except the unauthenticated auth endpoints and refresh.
- **Refresh is reactive and single-flight.** A `401` with `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` on any call
  triggers at most one in-flight `POST /auth/refresh`; concurrent callers await the same
  promise, then the original request is retried exactly once. A failed refresh (`401`) resolves
  every waiter as unauthenticated and does not retry — retrying a rotated token is precisely
  what FR-31 treats as theft. There is no proactive timer (AUTH-003 open question, resolved
  here for run 1).
- Transport failure and timeout → `ApiFailure{kind:"network"}`, unchanged.
- `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED` → `retryAfterSeconds` from `Retry-After`, default 30.
- The SPA never reads a cookie and never stores a token.

### 8.3 i18n ownership for this run

| File | Owner |
|---|---|
| `libs/i18n/locales/{en-US,vi-VN}.json` (server, keyed by error code) | `plat-audit-model` |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/errorMessages.ts` (code → SPA key map) | `plat-audit-model` |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/locales/{en-US,vi-VN}.json` (SPA catalogs) | `fe-auth-flows` |

`plat-audit-model` adds `errorMessages.ts` entries pointing at
`errors.auth_email_unverified` and `errors.auth_link_invalid`; **`fe-auth-flows` adds those two
keys to both SPA catalogs**, along with everything under `auth.*` its screens need. The map may
name a key before the catalog has it — the parity script checks the two catalogs against each
other, and `fe-auth-flows`'s done-criteria is where parity must hold.

`landing.*` keys are frozen this run. The landing slice is not modified at all.
